verdict.rationale: Apify's client exposes both synchronous run-and-wait patterns (actor.call()) and asynchronous notification via webhooks when a run finishes, plus log streaming for partial visibility during a run, which together give some control over when results are retrieved. However there is no explicit documentation of a latency/completeness tradeoff mechanism (e.g., a wait-timeout or partial-dataset-return parameter) that lets a developer explicitly choose faster-but-incomplete vs slower-but-complete results. Missing for 10: explicit timeout/waitForFinish parameter documentation, partial-result/early-return API semantics, and independent confirmation of this tradeoff being used in practice.
